newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian oil and gas shipyard workers start strike.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian oil and gas shipyard workers start strike.

text.p: Workers at French-owned ship building and repair firm CARENA in Ivory Coast's commercial capital went on strike on Wednesday over pay, officials said.
CARENA services the offshore oil and gas exploration and production sector.
The Ivorian ship builders and repairers union SYLICOTRA said it demanded pay in line with naval repair and construction trades instead of mechanical industry rates.
CARENA, which handles 200 ships a year for mainly American and European clients, dismissed the strike as "illegal".
"They want a naval pay scale which does not exist," said Administration and Finance Director Michel Raguier, adding that rates paid were in line with Ivorian collective agreements.
CARENA, owned by 50 percent shareholding French firms Bollore and Ateliers des Chantiers du Havre, employs 340 staff, with another 260 on contractual terms, including 20 expatriates.
